items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: my dad was a great trumpet player, played lead trumpet like Conrad Gozzo

ctx.x: In a song that perhaps could then be transferred to an improvisation.

Well when I was a kid I asked my dad how do you play jazz. And my dad was a great trumpet player, played lead trumpet like Conrad Gozzo and jazz like Louis, and he was a conductor of classical music. He said, “Just embellish the melody like Louis.” And I did that. And that was [inaudible] melody like Louis. And really I wrote in the liner notes to my Charlie Parker with Strings album, I carried that philosophy of embellishing the melody even when it got more advanced like Charlie Parker, ‘cause what Charlie…
